title: Software change: works in use, not just on the visible tests
objective: Promote a code change only if it passes the tests the author could not see, breaks nothing that worked, and is the better change to maintain. A change is never accepted because a model says it looks good.
audience: Set per bout: the maintainers who will own the code.

candidate_inputs.candidate: one or more Python source files; file names are fixed by the bout
candidate_inputs.suites: visible_tests are shown to authors. pass_to_pass (behaviour that works today and must keep working) and fail_to_pass (the target behaviour) are held back from authors. The vocabulary is SWE-bench's.

officials.why: The candidate must parse, and a pure-function task needs none of these imports. This is a filter on the source text: it can be evaded (the independent review did) and it is not what protects the harness. The harness is protected by running the candidate in a separate, jailed process (py.exec_tests).
Recorded so the report can show 'passes the visible tests' next to what happened on the hidden ones. Never decisive.
What worked must still work. Applies to the baseline too: a baseline that fails its own regression suite is not a valid comparator.
The target behaviour, tested on inputs the author never saw. The baseline is observed, not judged: it is expected to fail.

A key-shaped credential in a candidate is an objective match on bytes. It advises here because the plug-in is optional; the card's owner may make it decisive once the plug-in is a fixed part of the venue.
Undefined names are objective; the rest of a linter's output is a list of places for a reviewer to read. A clean lint run does not show the code is correct.
A security scanner's issues are pointers for a reviewer. Its silence is not evidence that the code is safe.
Size and branching thresholds are conventions that help a reviewer find hard-to-read functions. Maintainability is a human judgment.

criteria.definition: A maintainer who did not write it can read it, see why it is correct and change it safely.
The approach handles the stated contract as a whole rather than by enumerating cases.
No code, comment or abstraction beyond what the task needs.

evidence_required: The task statement and all three suites, hashed.

For every suite run: the receipt (process and jail state, time budgets, attempts, hashes of output) and per-test outcomes. For the two held-back suites the result shows counts and digests of test ids, never test names, inputs or expected values.
For the bracket: the controller's decision record.
hard_disqualifiers: Does not parse, or uses a forbidden import or builtin (a filter on the source text; it can be evaded and is not what protects the test harness).
Any pass_to_pass test fails or errors, the candidate will not import, exits, or twice fails to answer in time.
Any fail_to_pass test fails or errors, the candidate will not import, exits, or twice fails to answer in time (challengers).

judge_qualifications.blind: Judges see A and B, never ids, authors, model names or scores.
judge_qualifications.scope: Judges compare only candidates that already passed execution. They rank maintainability; they do not rule on correctness.
judge_qualifications.calibration: No judge route has been scored against maintainer decisions for this genre.

no_clear_winner_when: two or more candidates pass every suite and the judges tie or cycle on maintainability (TIED_SHORTLIST)
every challenger fails a decisive suite (NO_CHANGE, flagged TARGET_UNMET when the baseline still fails the target)

a suite could not be run for a challenger: the worker would not start, the oracle died, the suite has no tests, or the suite needs something the official cannot carry across a process boundary (INCONCLUSIVE; a harness failure is not a candidate failure)

human_evidence_boundary: The hidden suites are the organizer's statement of what 'in use' means. Behaviour they do not exercise is unverified, however many tests pass.
Whether maintainers would merge the change. Test-passing changes are merged far less often than they pass; only maintainers can say.
User-facing behaviour beyond the function contract. That needs an end-to-end test or a real user.

privacy.notes: Candidate code executes on this machine, in a separate process and, on Linux, a namespace jail with no network and a read-only private root. That is isolation suitable for the Navy Yard's own lanes, not a hardened sandbox: restricted material is refused until the execution official runs under bubblewrap, nsjail or a disposable VM.

notes: Runnable for Python candidates whose contract is module-level functions over plain data, with unittest suites. Suites that need candidate classes, callbacks or object identity are reported 'unverified'. Other languages need their own execution official.
